newsitem.title: USA: Kmart stock falls on lower profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: Kmart stock falls on lower profit outlook.

text.p: The stock of Kmart Corp. fell in active trading Thursday, a day after the nation's third-largest retailer said its second-quarter profits will fall due to continued high markdowns on women's apparel.
Morgan Stanley, which had previously recommended the stock as a "strong buy," downgraded it to "outperform."
The stock fell 69 cents to $10.81 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most active issue at midafternoon.
Kmart, based in Troy, Mich., said Wednesday its second-quarter earnings will be less than its year-ago profit of $34 million, or 7 cents a share.

"Currently, we expect that Kmart will report a profitable second quarter, but below last year's performance," Kmart Chairman Floyd Hall said in a statement accompanying the retailer's June sales results.
Last year's meagre second-quarter profit broke a three-year string of declining profits and losses for the retailer, which has faced a number of setbacks on its road to recovery.
